UK COMMERCIAL GUIDES

Considering a talking parrot?

Speech is a possibility, not a promise. Choose a bird whose everyday needs you can support.

A talking reputation is not an individual guarantee

People often search for talking parrots when exploring African greys, Amazons or other companions. Vocal learning varies between individuals and environments. A bird associated with a talking species may not develop speech, and an existing vocabulary may not be used in a new home.

The important test is whether you would still want to care for the bird if it never spoke. Use the African parrot guide and Amazon guide to consider routine, diet, exercise and noise alongside vocal interest.

Ask about actual behaviour

If an individual bird is described as talking, ask what has been observed and in which setting. Request context about its normal vocalisation rather than treating a short recording as proof of what it will do all day. Talking ability should not replace questions about age, history, handling and current care.

Remember that speech and other calls can coexist. A bird that learns words can also make loud natural sounds. Discuss noise tolerance with everyone sharing the household.

Make a suitable match first

Compare the African grey buying questions and Amazon buying questions before deciding on a species. Do not assume that a small bird is incapable of vocal learning or that a large bird will speak.

When enquiring, include your routine, experience and available space. Ask about the individual’s needs and vocal behaviour without requesting a guaranteed future skill.
